newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit unmoved despite higher money supply data.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit unmoved despite higher money supply data.

text.p: The ringgit did not react to higher money supply growth for July as players again preferred to keep firmly to the sidelines, dealers said.
They said the data served to reinforce expectations that Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) will continue to keep interest rates up until the end of the year.
"For the time being, BNM won't do anything because credit growth is still on high side," said Jimmy Koh, economist at research house I.D.E.A.
At the 1000 GMT local close, ringgit was at 2.4933/38 per dollar against 2.4930/40 on Friday.
Bank Negara said broad money M3 expanded by 25.1 percent year-on-year against 22.9 percent growth in June.
"The ringgit saw interbank play. People were not excited by anything," said a Singapore-based dealer.
In the interbank market, the overnight rate ended unchanged at 8.7 percent as funds remained fairly tight at the short-end, dealers said.
The one-month rate was at 7.50/60 percent from 7.20/60 previously.
